Six young women of varying body shapes and sizes stand in a row in black leotards, holding 
hands. Positive phrases are written on their arms and legs (generous, kindness, be positive, 
patience, tolerance, speak out, empathy, fairness, get help, acceptance, friendship, stand up, 
accept, happy, be supportive, respect listen). 
Combatting weight stigma and discrimination will require change on many levels. Governments can 
include weight as a category covered in anti-discrimination laws. Anti-bullying efforts at the school 
level should include policies on harassment and bullying related to weight. Healthcare should include 
reimbursement for obesity treatment, and weight bias training should be required for healthcare 
providers. Providers should ensure that their facilities are comfortable and welcoming to people of 
all sizes, and that they offer evidence-based care and treatment options to all patients, regardless 
of their size. And education and awareness about weight bias on an individual level will help change 
negative attitudes toward overweight and obesity.30,32
